answer: Give every newcomer a silent probationary season: it works in the open, but no one tells it which jobs are scored, and standing is granted only at the season's end, when strangers grade its whole public record at once. A walnut-shell trick — performing only while watched — fails, because the watch never announces itself. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues only from a full season of honest work, and the kernel of the rule is simple: a farm must sustain every fake, every day, with no shortcuts, while honest agents simply do their jobs and pass.
